title: AdaptRouter: Continual Learning to Route across Evolving Tasks and Models
scope: Current manuscript tables and figures, synchronized 2026-11-14. Reported point estimates; no new training or model calls.
api_cost_note: List-price cost of selected successful expert answers; excludes training, judges, router compute and unknown failed-attempt invoices. Router-R1 uses the documented conservative high-side comparison policy.
open_cost_note: Parameter-weighted input/output token proxy relative to Qwen3.5-9B (thinking); not dollar cost or wall time.
training_note: Open-weight main and continual studies use feedback-based RL. API routers are fully finetuned using cached feedback with soft-target cross-entropy plus expected regret (lambda=0.02, tau=0.05).
coverage_note: Open and API suites are different test sets; their averages are not directly comparable. Max-effort reference rows are partial external results, not complete matched local runs.
continual_note: All four stages are reported as per-task accuracies, with no replay of earlier training data. Full-finetuning rows are from the main table; LoRA variants are from the appendix.
ablation_note: Full model trained on one GPU, ablations on eight. The evaluation includes the documented 400-question training overlap; it is not a wholly independent held-out test.
precision_note: Numbers reproduce displayed table precision. Narrative summaries are not used to overwrite explicit table cells.
pool_note: One JevAny-0.8B pointer head is trained sequentially on M3, M5 and M10, inheriting the previous head and AdamW state. Each stage adds 500 updates on the same 400 training questions; evaluation uses the same disjoint 2,280 questions.
exploration_note: Independent M10 routers, 500 updates each. All: the 2,280 pool-study test questions; Held-out 10%: fixed question families never explored; Remain Unseen: all questions not explored by that run. Values follow the manuscript table; these subsets have distinct denominators.
